titulo: Your plan: one step at a time
titulo_curto: Your plan and the final video
lead: You’ve seen the four steps. Now make a dated plan, do the exercises in order, and move up only when “done when” is true.
objetivo: leave with a dated action plan and know how to tell whether each step is solid.

aprende.t: Review the whole journey in a video

secoes.sub: The four steps, the 23 exercises, and what each step delivers. Click an exercise to see “done when.”

degraus.saida: An agent working in your folder, with a safety net.
degraus.passo: The foundation for everything. Six exercises take you from your first mkdir to an agent reading your files and citing its sources. Without this step in place, the other three get stuck.

degraus.saida: Your own assistant, with memory and a routine in use.
degraus.passo: Requires step 1 (terminal, folders, and .env). From the plan in meu-jarvis.md to a routine used five days in a row; the memory test takes two days.

degraus.saida: Tasks running overnight, with a gate on what matters.
degraus.passo: Requires steps 1 and 2. The queue on paper and the homemade queue come before the bot; a night of tasks shows how many finish correctly on the first try.

degraus.saida: A niche channel with sources on screen and a gated schedule.
degraus.passo: Requires the previous three steps: without a queue and a gate, automating social media means posting the wrong thing faster. It ends with a week of manual approval.

resultado.titulo: At the end of the training
resultado.texto: An agent in your folder, your own assistant, a queue with gates, and a channel with sources on screen.

rolagem_fim.texto: Four steps in order, each with its own exercise list and a verifiable criterion. Move up only when “done when” for the previous step is true.

secoes.legenda: Required order: each step builds on what the previous one set up.

secoes.sub: Choose a start date and how much time you have each week. The plan accounts for exercises that require real days of use.

txt.travou: ## What got stuck and the rule I created

itens.texto: The benefit doesn’t come from a new model. It comes from moving work out of chat and into a folder with rules, Git, and secrets kept out of the text.
Terminal, assistant, queue, and social media. Each one builds on the previous step, and “done when” tells you when to move up.
A gate before what matters, refusals that become rules, and sources on screen. Automation doesn’t mean letting go.

secoes.sub: Two and a half minutes to review the four steps before you start.
Four questions about the entire training.

perguntas.p: What is the order of the steps?
perguntas.explica: Terminal, assistant (Jarvis), queues, and social media. Each step builds on the previous one.

opcoes: That the exercise took the stated amount of time.
A verifiable criterion for knowing whether you can move on.
That the agent won’t make mistakes.
That the certificate has been issued.
perguntas.explica: It’s the criterion you check: move on to the next exercise only when it’s true.

perguntas.p: Which of these should never go in a project text file?
perguntas.explica: Tokens and keys belong only in .env, which is in .gitignore. This applies from step 1 through step 4.

perguntas.p: A workflow will publish on the company’s behalf every morning. What must be in place at the start?
perguntas.explica: Without a queue and a gate, automating social media means posting the wrong thing faster. The gate only comes out after several days in a row without a refusal.
